**Job Requisition ID #

**26WD99977

**Business Consultant - AECO Technical Advisory

****Position Overview

**Autodesk Consulting is looking for a Business Consultant to join our Northern Europe team. This remote role supports strategic customers across the region.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining business consulting, AECO industry expertise and executive advisory. You’ll work with some of Autodesk’s largest customers to shape transformation strategies, define target operating models, and develop business cases and roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

You’ll advise senior leaders, structure complex business challenges and lead strategic advisory engagements from discovery through executive decision-making. While you won’t configure or implement solutions, you’ll understand how Autodesk and complementary technologies fit within customers’ broader business and technology ecosystems, partnering with technical specialists to turn strategy into actionable delivery plans.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders and transformation teams, acting as a strategic advisor throughout the engagement

• Understand customer objectives, challenges and operating context to define outcome-driven transformation strategies

• Assess operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, data and digital workflows to identify opportunities for improvement

• Define target-state operating models, transformation roadmaps, business cases, success measures and benefits realization plans

• Lead executive workshops, facilitate decision-making and align stakeholders across complex organizations

• Advise customers on how Autodesk and complementary AECO technologies support business outcomes through effective workflows, data management and interoperability

• Identify and prioritize opportunities for data, automation and AI based on business value, organizational readiness, governance and adoption

• Partner with Solution Architects, technical consultants and customer-facing teams to shape advisory engagements, validate strategic recommendations and develop credible delivery roadmaps

**Minimum Qualifications

**

• Substantial experience in AECO, management consulting or business transformation, with a proven track record of independently leading complex strategy and transformation engagements

• Deep expertise in at least one of the following: construction, infrastructure, engineering consultancy, utilities, or a closely related project-based, asset-intensive industry

• Strong working knowledge of Autodesk technologies or comparable AECO tool ecosystems, with the ability to discuss capabilities, workflow fit, data, interoperability and business value. Hands-on implementation expertise is not required

• Strong understanding of operating models, organizational change, governance, business cases and benefits realization

• Practical understanding of data-centric workflows, enterprise systems, automation, responsible AI and technology adoption

• Ability to lead through influence across cross-functional and international teams, with excellent communication and executive presentation skills

• Fluent English is required. Dutch and other European languages are highly valued

• Willingness to travel to customer meetings and Autodesk events across Northern Europe (up to 50%)

• Proven experience advising executives, structuring complex problems, facilitating high-stakes workshops and driving decisions

****Learn More

******About Autodesk

**Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

**Salary transparency

**Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For Netherlands based roles, we expect a starting base salary between 69,000 EUR and 101,200 EUR Annual. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Sales Careers

**Working in sales at Autodesk allows you to build meaningful relationships with customers while growing your career. Join us and help make a better, more sustainable world. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/careers/sales

**Belonging

**We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: **https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

****In-Person Onboarding and Identity Verification

**This role may require in-person onboarding and/or in-person ID verification.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

If so, we are looking for dedicated, curious, and highly motivated graduates to join the DFDS Graduate Programme starting in September 2027.

**Be part of the movement - and play your part

**About The Role The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Ferry Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the operational and commercial sides of our Ferry Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

Ferry Operations offers broad end-to-end exposure with sustainability, standardisation, and digitalisation at the heart of everything we do.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Help design and develop the vessels of tomorrow, supporting our green transition through electrification, ammonia, and green methanol initiatives.

• Support the operation and maintenance of our fleet of more than 70 RoRo, RoPax, and passenger vessels, covering everything from dry dock planning to crisis management and contingency handling.

• Contribute to our standardisation and digitalisation journey across eight owned terminals and more than 20 third-party terminals, where safety remains our highest priority.

• Support fleet planning, equipment optimisation, and our intercontinental rail setup, connecting ferry and logistics operations across our network.

In the commercial part of our Ferry Division, you will work alongside colleagues across Europe, supporting both B2B and B2C markets.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Support local and global sales teams and assist with key account management, ensuring our network is successfully marketed and sold across regions.

• Drive continuous improvement in customer service and booking processes through standardisation and digitalisation initiatives.

• Collaborate with IT teams to enhance and optimise our digital customer offerings.

• Work with operational teams to optimise routes and vessel capacity to meet customer demand.

• Support revenue management activities, including pricing optimisation and commercial performance analysis.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and engage with customers, suppliers, and partners throughout the maritime value chain. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

Alongside hands-on experience at DFDS, you will participate in the Danish Shipping Education Programme, delivered by Danish Shipping. This programme consists of webinars, four seminars in Denmark, and one international seminar, covering key topics across the maritime industry.

****About You

****At DFDS, we believe the strongest teams are built on diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have graduated from a relevant master’s degree by the start of the Graduate Programme in September 2027, preferably within maritime studies, supply chain, freight forwarding, logistics, sustainability, business, finance, engineering, or a related field.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

Working at DFDS **Join the movement and grow with us

**As part of the DFDS Graduate Programme, you will become part of a strong graduate network across the company and build valuable connections across our international business. We offer a steep learning curve, meaningful responsibility from day one, and three interesting rotations designed to accelerate your professional development.

Are we a match? Apply now.  If your skills, experience, aspirations, and personality match this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Please Apply By Uploading Your CV no Later Than 30 November 2026. When Applying, You’re Also Asked To Answer The Following Questions:

• Why are you interested in joining the DFDS Graduate Programme?

• How will the programme help kickstart your career?

• How do you expect to contribute to the programme and DFDS?

• What do you believe will be your biggest challenge(s) during the programme?

**We look forward to hearing from you.

**Visit our Graduate site here to learn more and meet some of our people.

Join our Sitaware Extensions Program and help deliver customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, from sensor interfaces to radio drivers. As Senior Software Developer, you will combine software design, implementation and testing in a close-knit team working in an exciting domain.

The job

You will contribute to the delivery of high-quality integrations and extensions, from requirements analysis through software design, implementation and testing. Beyond hands-on development, you will help apply and improve our development process, and share your knowledge to support the team's growth.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Designing, implementing, documenting and debugging features, working primarily on back-end development (Java) and occasionally on front-end development (Angular)

• Analysing requirements, breaking them into technical tasks, and clarifying acceptance criteria

• Implementing and troubleshooting interfaces to hardware and external systems, such as sensors and radio interfaces

• Developing and maintaining unit and integration tests, and designing for testability

• Identifying issues and recommending improvements to code, tooling, pipelines and processes

Joining the team

You will be part of the Product Extension Team of around seven developers, test engineers and architects, part of the Sitaware Extensions Program within Defence Services. The team delivers customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, focusing on software- and hardware-related integrations such as sensor interfaces, radio drivers and interoperability with external systems, and continuously improves its own testing and development practices, methods and tools. This is a newly created position, so you will have real scope to shape how the role develops as the team continues to grow.

Your qualifications

To succeed in this role, you bring several years of software development experience gained in a structured, team-based environment, along with:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Software Technology or similar

• Hands-on experience with Java (or a related object-oriented technology) for backend development, and Angular (or a similar modern framework) for frontend development

• Fluent English; Danish is a nice-to-have

Alongside this, we value:

• Strong analytical abilities, with a focused and open mindset

• The ability to communicate intent and purpose clearly, both in writing and conversation

• Enjoys collaborating closely within a cross-functional team

Onboarding includes two three-day stays in Aarhus, and you should expect occasional travel of around two to ten days a year, mostly within Europe. Some onsite hardware testing may also be required, depending on integration needs.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Copenhagen

When you join us in Copenhagen, you're not just getting a desk at one of the city's best locations—you are stepping into a workplace where community matters. Our Employees Club keeps things lively with monthly social events, and our office catering makes sure you are always well taken care of. Whether you are into casual games or just good company, you will find both at our foosball table or during our relaxed Friday bar gatherings.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Andreas Markussen, Senior Manager.

**💰 🇩🇰 up to 46,000 DKK gross/month (depending on seniority level)

**Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

**A Brief Overview Of Our Tech Stack

**

• Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

**If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

**AI Competency

• You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

Please send us your application in English.

To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

Please note that we don't accept unsolicited applications from headhunters or recruitment agencies. Unsolicited applications sent to our company or co-workers are considered to be the property of Monta, and we won't agree to pay any referral compensation or recruiter fee without a signed agreement.

Find out more by visiting https://monta.com/uk/careers/

Monta is building the platform that powers the future of EV charging. We connect hardware, software, businesses, and drivers into one seamless ecosystem. Our mission is to make charging simple, reliable, and scalable for everyone.

HR Manager

Take responsibility for HR operations, employee development and people management in an international project organisation.

Copenhagen Group A/S is a Danish project-driven company with a strong international profile.

We tender for and manage complex projects for international organisations and national authorities and, as the parent company of several specialised subsidiaries, provide the shared structure that ensures consistency across the Group.

Our activities span different markets, projects and stakeholders, placing high demands on structured HR processes and effective people management.

To support this, we are looking for an experienced and proactive HR Manager to take overall responsibility for HR activities and contribute to the continued development of the organisation.

Your Responsibilities

You will be responsible for managing and developing HR activities across Copenhagen Group, ensuring consistent and effective processes that support employees and management.

Your responsibilities will include personnel administration and the development and maintenance of HR policies, procedures and systems.

You will work closely with management on employee relations, organisational development, employee engagement, training and professional development

You will also ensure compliance with relevant employment legislation, maintain accurate employee records and provide management with HR data and guidance to support informed decision-making.

The role requires you to work independently, take ownership of HR processes and initiatives, and promote a positive working environment across the Group.

Your Background

We are looking for someone with proven experience in HR management or a similar role, including responsibility for HR processes, employee relations and personnel administration.

You have solid knowledge of Danish employment legislation and HR best practices, along with practical experience in recruitment, HR systems and employee development.

You are structured, reliable and proactive, with strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to balance strategic initiatives with day-to-day responsibilities.

You have excellent interpersonal skills, exercise sound judgement and handle confidential matters with professionalism and discretion.

You communicate fluently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing.

A relevant educational background in HR, business administration or a related field is required.

Practical Information

The position is based at our office in Copenhagen.

We offer a key position with a high degree of independence and responsibility, where you will have significant influence on HR practices and organisational development across Copenhagen Group.

Salary will reflect qualifications and experience.

Employment is conditional upon obtaining the required security clearance.

Are you ready to combine hands-on IT support with technical development in an international shipping company?

At Clipper Bulk, we are looking for an IT Operations & Support Specialist to join our IT team at our headquarters in Copenhagen.

This is an opportunity to become a key part of our IT function, ensuring reliable day-to-day support while gradually taking on broader responsibilities within IT operations, Microsoft 365 and infrastructure.

As IT Operations & Support Specialist, you will play an important role in keeping our IT environment running smoothly and supporting colleagues across the organisation. You will take ownership of daily IT support in close collaboration with the rest of the IT team, while also contributing to the maintenance, improvement and development of our IT systems.

Over time, you will have the opportunity to take on greater responsibility for operational tasks and smaller IT projects.

What will be your responsibilities:

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

• Providing hands-on IT support and troubleshooting for colleagues

• Managing and maintaining Microsoft 365 services, including Entra ID, Exchange Online and Intune

• Supporting device management, user administration and employee onboarding and offboarding

• Handling day-to-day IT operational tasks and ensuring system stability

• Supporting identity and access management, endpoint security and IT infrastructure

• Maintaining IT documentation, procedures and best practices

• Identifying opportunities to improve and automate IT processes

• Participating in smaller IT operations and infrastructure projects

• Collaborating with internal stakeholders and external IT service providers

What we are looking for:

At Clipper, our employees shape our work environment, so bringing a positive attitude is essential.

We are looking for someone who genuinely enjoys both IT support and technical operations. You are comfortable taking responsibility for day-to-day support, but you are also curious about the technology behind the systems and motivated to expand your technical capabilities. You don't just wait for the next support ticket. You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement and follow tasks through to completion.

We imagine that you bring:

• Practical experience with IT support and technical troubleshooting

• Experience with Microsoft 365 administration, including Entra ID and related services

• Knowledge of Microsoft Intune, endpoint management and Windows client administration

• A good understanding of user management, access rights and IT security principles

• A structured and independent approach to solving technical challenges

• Good communication skills and a service-minded attitude

• Strong English communication skills, both written and spoken

• Experience with IT security and endpoint security solutions, network infrastructure, PowerShell, IT automation, identity and access management, IT projects or AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot would be an advantage, but is not a requirement

• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience

If you’re enthusiastic about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with each qualification, we still encourage you to apply. You could be the ideal candidate for this position, or for another opportunity with us.

What you will love about us

At Clipper, you will become part of a growing and professional work environment where we strive to be the best. We offer:

• A varied role combining hands-on support, IT operations and technical development.

• The opportunity to gradually expand your responsibilities and technical expertise.

• Close collaboration with experienced IT colleagues.

• An international working environment with colleagues across our global offices.

• A welcoming and inclusive work environment with a variety of socal, sports, and cultural events throughout the year

• Attractive employee benefits, including pension, health, dental and critical ilness insurance

• Beautiful office facilities in Nordhavn, located near the metro with on-site parking, delicious lunch arangement and access to fitness facilities and a personal trainer.

Application and recruitment process:

Please submit your CV and cover letter through our application portal by 29th November 2026.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and interviews will be treated with full discretion.

The recruitment process consists of two interview rounds. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a first interview conducted via video call. Candidates progressing to the second round will be invited to an in-person interview and asked to complete a personality assessment and a logical reasoning test beforehand. Confidential reference checks will be conducted for final candidates.

Learn more about Clipper at clipper-bulk.com, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

Clipper is an industry leader in dry bulk, an operator, a pool manager, and a specialist in steel services. We operate a modern fleet of approximately 120 handysize and supramax vessels, transporting a wide range of cargo from dry bulk to break bulk. Clipper is commercially headquartered in Copenhagen and employs a staff of around 100 onshore worldwide__. We are a global workplace built on five shared values: Dependable, Curious, Collaboration, Hands-on and Family. We believe in learning from one another and welcome people with a growth mindset and ambition.

Sustainability initiatives - we strive to make a positive impact. As a maritime player with a global presence at sea and onshore, we recognize our social, environmental, and ethical responsibility. We push for positive development by responsibly running our business and promoting sustainable business behavior in our network. Read more about sustainability initiatives on our website.

At Acodyne, you will help develop the software, high-power electronics, and robotic systems that bring our next generation of high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAS to life, moving between code, schematics, the lab bench, and real flight hardware.

Your Role

You Will Work Closely With Our CTO And Engineering Team On The Electrical And Software Systems That Power And Control Our Aircraft. From Firmware To High-power Distribution, This Is As Real As Engineering Gets. You Will

• 
Develop and test embedded software and firmware for flight-critical and ground systems (C/C++, Python)

• 
Design, build, and test high-power electronics such as power distribution, battery systems, and motor drives

• 
Integrate sensors, actuators, and robotic/autonomous subsystems into the aircraft and ground equipment

• 
Develop tools for test automation, data logging, and analysis

• 
Bring up, debug, and validate hardware on the bench and during flight tests

• 
Document designs, code, and test results for certification purposes

**About You

**You enjoy writing code as much as holding an oscilloscope probe or a soldering iron. You're the type who builds things outside class and wants to take that to the next level. You likely:

• 
Are currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, software/computer engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or similar

• 
Have programming experience in C/C++ and/or Python

• 
Have a solid understanding of electronics and circuit design

• 
Enjoy hands-on lab work, prototyping, and debugging real hardware

• 
Are curious about UAVs, robotics, or high-performance systems

• 
Are proactive, independent, and eager to learn fast

**Nice To Have

**

• 
Experience with power electronics, high-voltage systems, motor control, or battery management systems (BMS)

• 
Experience with embedded platforms (STM32, ARM, etc.), RTOS, or communication buses (CAN, UART, SPI, I²C)

• 
Exposure to ROS, PX4/ArduPilot, or control and autonomy algorithms

• 
PCB design experience (KiCad, Altium, etc.)

**About Acodyne

**We are a UAS company developing heavy-lift, high-speed eVTOL UAS for defence and industrial logistics. We are currently 18 people, based at our workshop at Avedøre Airfield, and plan to double our team in the next year.

**About The Internship

**

• 
Duration: Full-time for 5–6 months, with start in January/February 2027.

• 
Time off: 2.08 vacation days per month + Danish public holidays.

• 
Location: Avedøre Flyveplads, workshop-based, approximately 45 minutes by public transport from Copenhagen city center.

• 
Compensation: DKK 6,000-8,000 per month before tax. Please note this is a contribution to living and transport. It will likely not cover full living costs. Interns are expected to supplement with grants or other funding.

• 
Visa: Acodyne is unfortunately not able to help obtain a work visa. It is expected that the candidate has a legal right to work in Denmark.

• 
Please note: The internship opportunity is intended for currently enrolled students who wish to gain relevant work experience as part of their studies. We particularly encourage applications from students who are able to use the internship as an integrated part of their degree programme, for example through ECTS credits, a project-based internship, or another formal study-related arrangement.

jobs.occupation: Women’s Academy 2027: Insights into the financial sector
jobs.description:
Step inside the world of finance and explore what happens on a busy trading floor, how major companies are financed and how a bank manages risk in changing markets and society. Women’s Academy is an 8-week student programme at Danske Bank’s headquarters, designed to give you first-hand insight into Large Corporates & Institutions and Group Risk & Compliance.

What you will be doing

Across eight weekly sessions, you will meet specialists from across Danske Bank who will introduce you to their work, share real perspectives from the industry and involve you in relevant business topics.

During the programme, you will:

• 
Explore areas such as Corporate Banking, Markets, Corporate Finance, Risk and Compliance

• 
Gain insight into how different parts of Danske Bank work together

• 
Work with practical topics linked to finance, risk and business decisions

• 
Hear directly from people working in the financial sector

• 
Meet other students who are curious about finance

• 
Become part of the Women’s Academy community

• 
Take part in a celebratory dinner at the end of the programme

• 
Receive a certificate of participation upon completing the Academy

The Academy was created to encourage more women to explore finance. Women are still underrepresented in several parts of the sector, and by opening our doors, sharing knowledge and providing access to role models, we want to make finance feel more accessible to a broader range of students.

About you

We welcome applications from university students between the second year of their bachelor’s degree and the second year of their master’s degree.

You do not need previous experience in banking or finance. You also do not need to know whether finance is the right career path for you yet. The Academy is a place to explore the sector from within and discover what captures your interest.

We are looking for students who:

• 
Are curious about finance, business, markets or risk

• 
Want to learn more about career opportunities in the financial sector

• 
Are motivated to take an active part in discussions and sessions

• 
Bring an open mindset and a willingness to explore new topics

• 
Come from any academic background and are interested in learning from others

Practical information

• 
Programme period: 8 weeks in Q1 2027

• 
Duration: Eight weekly sessions of approximately three hours

• 
Location: Danske Bank headquarters, Copenhagen

• 
Application window: 2 November-23 November

• 
Attendance: Participants are expected to attend all eight sessions

What we offer you

You will get a unique opportunity to experience the financial sector from the inside, meet specialists from across Danske Bank and build your understanding of how finance connects to companies, markets and society. You will also become part of a student community and gain access to people who can share their experiences, career paths and advice.

Are you ready to explore finance?

To apply, please submit your CV and answer five short questions about your motivation, what makes you curious about finance and what you hope to gain from Women’s Academy. Instead of submitting a cover letter, we would like to get to know your perspective through your answers. There are no right or wrong answers, and previous experience in banking or finance is not required. We encourage you to respond openly and honestly, drawing on the experiences that are meaningful to you, whether they come from your studies, work, interests or personal life.

• 
Tell us briefly about yourself and what currently interests you.

Maximum 100 words

• 
What motivated you to apply for Women’s Academy, and what makes you curious about the financial sector?

Maximum 150 words

• 
Tell us about something you have achieved that you are proud of. Why is it meaningful to you?

This can come from your studies, work, volunteering, hobbies or personal life. Maximum 150 words.

• 
What motivates or drives you when learning something new?

Maximum 100 words

• 
What do you hope to gain from Women’s Academy, and how would you contribute to the programme?

Maximum 150 words

For further information please contact:

• 
Victoria Witzeling, DEI Lead LC&I and BC, at viwi@danskebank.dk or +45 20 65 21 34

jobs.description:
Capital planning sits at the heart of how Danske Bank balances financial resilience with sustainable growth. As part of a close-knit analytical team, you will contribute to decisions that enable the bank to serve its customers and support its strategic ambitions. This is a role where your work genuinely matters and where you will build a solid foundation in capital management.

The Capital Planning team is part of Financial Resource Management in Group Treasury, sitting within Danske Bank's CFO area. The team of seven works on capital target setting, capital issuances, dividend decisions and macroeconomic stress testing. Your analyses and reports will receive close attention from the Executive Leadership Team, the Board of Directors and financial regulators. The atmosphere is collaborative, with knowledge sharing and learning woven into everyday working life, and the team takes pride in delivering high-quality work while enjoying the process.

More specifically, you will:

• Support monthly capital and MREL assessments and projections

• Strong analytical skills and a structured, detail-oriented approach

• Ability to communicate complex findings clearly in English

• Curious and collaborative, with an interest in learning and developing within the field

You will lead, or contribute to, audits of the Group’s second line of defence Regulatory Compliance function, assessing governance, risk management and controls across regulatory compliance.

In this role, you will:

• Plan and conduct audits covering areas such as compliance risk assessments and Group Wide Risk Assessments, risk-based activity planning, compliance oversight and monitoring, management information and reporting

• Perform audits of specific regulatory compliance risk areas, including market integrity and market abuse surveillance, conflicts of interest, regulatory engagement, conduct risk and emerging compliance risks associated with new technologies and AI

• Apply professional scepticism, data analytics and technology-enabled audit techniques to identify risk patterns, test controls and deliver impactful audit insights

• Engage confidently with stakeholders at all organisational levels, communicate audit conclusions clearly and concisely, and monitor the timely resolution of audit findings and risk mitigation actions

• Contribute to the continuous development of audit methodologies, data-driven auditing techniques and the use of AI-enabled tools within Group Internal Audit

About you

We imagine that you bring:

• Several years of experience in internal audit, compliance, external audit, consulting, risk management or a comparable role in financial services

• Strong understanding of regulatory compliance risks, governance frameworks and the role of a second line Regulatory Compliance function

• Ability to assess complex regulatory and governance topics and communicate clear, well-supported conclusions to senior stakeholders

• Strong communication, stakeholder management and project management skills

• Strong analytical skills and an interest in leveraging data analytics and technology-enabled auditing techniques

We welcome candidates who bring curiosity, professional judgement and a commitment to continuous learning. Familiarity with AI-enabled audit tools or specific regulatory areas such as market abuse surveillance, conduct risk or regulatory engagement would be an advantage, but is not a requirement.

What we offer you

We invest in your development through training that matches your career aspirations. You will work in a collaborative environment that values different perspectives, professional curiosity and innovative thinking.

As part of Group Internal Audit, you will deliver independent assurance, insight and foresight and gain a unique enterprise-wide perspective on Regulatory Compliance’s risks, governance and control practices across the Group.

Our hybrid working model supports 3 to 4 days per week in the office, enabling close collaboration, knowledge sharing and professional development.

Are you ready for the next step?

If you are motivated by understanding how regulatory compliance risks are managed at Group level and want to apply your experience in an independent assurance role, we would be pleased to hear from you. If you have any questions before applying, please reach out to hiring manager, Christoffer Øhauge Pedersen at chrpe@danskebank.dk.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 4 December 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

The Human-Centred Computing Section, Department of Computer Science, invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in Human-Computer Interaction.

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project
 Digital technologies increasingly mediate how people experience, understand and respond to their bodies. The PhD project will investigate the relationship between bodies, technology and chronic illness, with a particular focus on self-tracking technologies. The project will explore how people with chronic conditions engage with these technologies and how technologies shape interactions with informal caregivers and health professionals. The project will critically examine how these technologies enact particular understandings of bodily difference and chronic illness, and how such understandings intersect with broader social, cultural and political norms. Within this topic, the PhD student will have some freedom to shape the focus of their work and the research questions they are interested in.

  The project will employ qualitative, participatory and design-oriented methods, with a particular emphasis on co-design and Research through Design. Co-design will involve working collaboratively with people with chronic conditions and other relevant stakeholders to explore their experiences of their bodies and technologies, and to imagine and develop new forms of technological interaction. Through Research through Design, the PhD researcher will develop and study experimental technological prototypes as a way of investigating alternative ways of sensing, representing and interacting with bodies. Design will be used not only to develop technological artefacts, but also as a means of generating knowledge about societal norms around chronic illness and the relationship between people and technology.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of human-computer interaction (HCI). The ideal candidate should have a strong background in user-centred research methods, with some experience of working in a research environment. We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in conducting design processes and developing both screen-based and physical computing prototypes. It is expected that candidates will have an M.Sc. degree in a relevant technical, design, or social science discipline. In addition, the ideal candidate will be able to document research capabilities (e.g., a thesis, publication, or project portfolio), have strong recommendations from supervisors and mentors, and possess a high level of intellectual humility. Preferred candidates would have advanced Danish language proficiency.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 The PhD fellow will become a member of the Human-Centered Computing (HCC) research section at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science. Here, we aim to fundamentally understand and improve the relation between computational technology and people. We are currently the top-ranked HCI research group in Europe (https://csrankings.org/#/index?chi&europe). Our research focuses on using computing to support people’s activities and well-being; inventing new ways for people to interact with technology, and understanding how human capabilities are influenced by technology. At the HCC section, we are currently over 15 faculty members, and over 20 postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and research assistants. We hold joint weekly research meetings, many annual retreats, and have a thriving social environment from daily lunches to larger events. We attend the most important international conferences, such as CHI. We particularly value having a supportive and collegial work environment that values and encourages diversity. 

  Copenhagen is a vibrant city, with many cultural offerings and easy access to the rest of Europe. For more information about working in Denmark, consult International Staff Mobility.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tariq Andersen, Department of Computer Science, tariq@di.ku.dk. The PhD project is led by Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, Department of Computer Science, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Computer Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 

  Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculy of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Computer Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY FOR POSITION below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Research Statement (max. one page excl. references) detailing your desired research focus. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research project within the topic of designing self-tracking technologies for chronic conditions you would wish to explore. This should include specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature and, if relevant, your previous research, and the potential impact and applications of this research. As we are interested in your own ideas and writing style, please do not use generative AI. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if relevant) 	
• Contact information for up to two people who have agreed to provide a reference.   Application deadline: 
 The deadline for applications is 29 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Truck Drivers for DSV Contract Logistics Horsens
jobs.description:
Truck Driver – Warehouse Operations

The Job

We are looking for experienced Truck Drivers to join the warehouse team at DSV in Horsens.

We are looking for:

• 
Truck Driver for the shift 16:00–00:00

• 
Truck Driver for the shift 14:00–22:00

The team is responsible for picking and packing furniture using scanners, as well as ensuring that all goods are correctly placed on pallets. As the products are furniture, you must be able to handle larger and heavier items.

A key part of the role is replenishing stock from high storage locations to lower picking locations. It is therefore important that you are comfortable handling pallets at high storage levels while operating the reach truck from ground level.

Most of the work is carried out using a reach truck. We are looking for both experienced and less experienced Truck Drivers. Whether you already have extensive reach truck experience or are looking to further develop your skills, the most important thing is that you are motivated, eager to learn and ready to contribute to the team.

DSV also offer the opportunity to be cross-trained in other warehouse processes, allowing you to develop your skills and gain broader experience within the operation.

Your Daily Tasks Will Include

• 
Picking and packing furniture

• 
Using scanners for warehouse tasks

• 
Replenishing stock from high storage locations

• 
Placing goods correctly on pallets

• 
Handling larger and heavier packages

• 
Operating a reach truck safely and efficiently

Your Profile

You are productive, committed and have a strong work ethic. You have a positive attitude, are detail-oriented and focused on delivering high-quality work.

Furthermore, we expect that you:

• 
Hold a valid forklift certificate approved in Denmark

• 
Speak and understand English

• 
Think efficiently and work in a structured manner

• 
Can handle larger and heavier packages

Salary

• 146,75 DKK/hour + 10% Flexible benefits allowance (fritvalgstillæg) = 161,43 DKK/hour

Interested?

If this sounds interesting to you, we encourage you to apply today, as we conduct interviews on an ongoing basis.

Click "Apply for the job" to submit your application. If you do not already have a profile with Moment, you will be asked to create one as the first step in the application process.

We look forward to hearing from you!

The company

DSV Contract Logistics is located in Horsens and is an international company that offers global and competitive transport and logistics solutions of high quality.

Moment
